prose.name: Recovery: Militia Clasp on <Planet>
prose.briefing: A salvager's note says he left a militia clasp at the <SecondPlace> and never went back for it. Something has nested there since.

message.title: Militia Clasp
message.text: The stash is where he left it, intact. The name on the clasp is scratched away, but the number is not, and it traces to a dead man with a brother at the <Place>.

beats.objective: Take the clasp to his brother
beats.journal: I dug a militia clasp out of an infested stash and took it to the soldier's brother at the <Place>.

message.title: Returned
message.text: His brother reads the number off it before he has it to the light, then sets it on the shrine. He pays what he can.

beats.name: Family Shrine

beats.objective: Sell the clasp to the militia post
beats.journal: I dug a militia clasp out of an infested stash and sold it to a militia post for their unit's honours.

message.title: Sold
message.text: The quartermaster pays in full and sets it in the footlocker, between two others from his unit.

beats.name: Unit Footlocker

offer.journal: The clasp's militia number matches a dead soldier whose brother lives at the <Place>. A militia post wants it for their unit's honours and will pay more than he can. It's my call.
say: Word gets round. Heard you pulled a militia clasp out of that infested hole.
We keep the old unit's honours in a footlocker, so the new lot know whose post it is.
I'll pay more than his brother can.
offer._say: Jessica's message text, spoken (his 2026-10-12: the call should be radio, not a box). Two cuts and no new words: "I'm at the <ThirdPlace>." (a voice cannot say a token; the objective names the place) and the sign-off (the subtitle carries the speaker's name).
